_doc: Real-world equivalence factors for the dashboard's three headline meter readings. Nothing here is estimated, derived or rounded by this project: each value is a figure published by a named authority, recorded with the sentence it came from, the URL, and the date it was fetched. scripts/generate-dashboard.sh divides the ledger totals by these at generation time. Refresh by re-fetching the cited page and updating the value, _source and _recorded together — never one without the others.
_scope: These equivalences illustrate scale. They are not scope-matched: the ledger's CO2e is usage-only (inference electricity), while the EPA vehicle factor is tailpipe CO2e per mile. The comparison answers 'how big is this number' and nothing more.

energy.noun: days of an average U.S. home's electricity
energy.cite: EIA: average U.S. residential customer used 10,791 kWh in 2022
energy._source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, FAQ 'How much electricity does an average American home use?': "In 2022, the average annual amount of electricity sold to (purchased by) a U.S. residential electric-utility customer was 10,791 kilowatthours (kWh), an average of about 899 kWh per month." Page last updated 2024-01-08. https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=97&t=3 — fetched 2026-08-07.

water.cite: EPA WaterSense: 8-minute shower at 2.1 gal/min = 16.8 gal = 63.6 L
water._source: U.S. EPA WaterSense, 'Save Water and Energy by Showering Better': "The average shower lasts about eight minutes. Since the average showerhead has a water flow of 2.1 gallons per minute, each shower uses more than 16 gallons of water!" 8 min x 2.1 gal/min = 16.8 US gal; 16.8 x 3.785411784 = 63.6 L. https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2017-02/documents/ws-ourwater-shower-better-learning-resource_0.pdf — fetched 2026-08-07. cite_url points at the stable WaterSense showerheads page, which carries the same 2.5 gpm federal standard context.

co2.noun: miles driven in an average gasoline car
co2.cite: EPA: 3.93e-4 t CO2e per mile, 2022 fleet (22.8 mpg, 10,917 mi/yr)
co2._source: U.S. EPA, Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator — Calculations and References, 'Gasoline-powered passenger vehicles per mile': 3.93 x 10^-4 metric tons CO2e/mile, from a 2022 weighted-average combined fuel economy of 22.8 mpg and average annual VMT of 10,917 miles. 3.93e-4 t = 0.393 kg. https://www.epa.gov/energy/greenhouse-gases-equivalencies-calculator-calculations-and-references — fetched 2026-08-07.
